blinding_guess.why: A ships a unit test suite, uses an atomic mkstemp save and does stricter schema validation, which fits a more process-driven build.

notes: Both implementations meet the core spec: they refuse a double start, detect overlaps in log, format HH:MM:SS (including over 24h) and report per-project totals. B also refuses to start a session that would overlap an existing one and warns about double-counting in report, but it mixes timezone-aware now() with stored timestamps that load() accepts as naive, and that crashes. A rejects offset timestamps cleanly as a corrupt file. Probes ran on Python 3.9.6; P13 checks imports against an explicit stdlib allowlist because sys.stdlib_module_names is not available in 3.9.
